question: If Stage IV, a real-time rain product, replaces AORC on the issue day of each test-year onset, how many onsets do the saved wqa networks still warn of 1 day ahead?
outcome: With Stage IV rain (radar and gauge, the product a service at midnight would read) in place of AORC on the issue day of each of the 611 onsets, the three saved lstm_wqa networks warn of 294 (48%) against 313 with AORC (51%) and 114 with the rain table alone (19%): 90% of the AORC effect survives (95% interval 85% to 97% drawing onsets, 84% to 97% drawing issue days). With the level of AORC restored (Stage IV times 1.06) 319 are warned; with the last hour of the issue day taken out 275, with the last two hours 255. On the issue days of all 12 basins (the warnings issued when the river was low; Stage IV in every basin on those days) Stage IV gives 291 hits and 97 false warnings (25% of the warnings) against 313 hits and 132 false warnings (30%) with AORC, and with the level of AORC restored 318 and 123 (28%). The count is more sensitive to whether the issue day was a heavy-rain day than to its exact rain: with the Stage IV rain of another onset of the same basin in its place the networks still warn of 284 (280 to 291 in 10 draws), with the AORC rain of an ordinary day 34, with no rain 11. The mean absolute error of the forecast on the onset days, which does depend on the exact rain, is 4.64 mm/day with AORC, 4.64 with Stage IV, 5.62 with another onset's Stage IV rain, 6.68 with an ordinary day's rain and 5.83 with the rain table alone.
honesty_points: the networks were trained on AORC (hours before 2002 disaggregated daily totals); Stage IV is substituted at forecast time only, and nothing is said about training on Stage IV

Stage IV covers 2002 onward, all test years; the issue days are the days before the onsets, so the false warnings are tested only on the issue days of all basins (issue_days_of_all_basins), not on days without any onset
the one-hour delay of Stage IV is not simulated, except by the variants that take the last hour or the last two hours of the issue day out

the count of onsets warned is a coarse test of whether Stage IV carries the same information as AORC: the controls show that it falls little when the rain of another onset day of the same basin is put in its place (onset days are all heavy-rain days); the fit of the forecasts to the observed flow on the onset days (fit_on_the_onset_days) and the controls are what separate 'heavy rain' from 'the rain of that day'

the Iowa Mesonet archive holds first postings or later versions of each hour (not established); hours the archive lacks, or in which no cell of the basin has radar coverage, are replaced by the AORC hour (fallback)
